title: Can Kashmir Learn From India’s Gen Z Movement?
author: Anando Bhakto
text:
People gather during a protest organized by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, India, demanding accountability over alleged examination irregularities and education reforms, July 19, 2026.
Credit: Arnav Pratap Singh / Shutterstock.com
On August 14, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah warned New Delhi of a potential Gen Z protest in the restive Himalayan region, while cataloguing the lieutenant governor’s endless attritions against his government – most recently the stalling on a reservation report that seeks to redress grievances over the open-merit category. On September 2, Abdullah’s Cabinet ministers descended onto Srinagar’s streets. Placards in hands, which named in bold, black letters the Narendra Modi regime’s repeated political incursions in Kashmir, they marched toward the headquarters of the Bharatiya Janata Party, the Hindu-nationalist party Modi heads. The demonstration was scuppered within minutes, with the police, which reports to the lieutenant governor, dashing on them. After a scuffle, the ministers were shoved inside vans like common criminals.[...]
